correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the incidence argument in RESULT.md lines 21–42. For distinct shifts t<u each common pattern site s gives a different ordered increasing pair (s+t,s+u) of difference u−t. Of r+2 different counts at least r are at least two. The r selected blocks therefore have total size L≥r(r+3)/2. If d_s counts blocks through s, summing d_s(d_s−1) counts ordered intersecting block pairs with weight at most g per ordered pair, so Cauchy–Schwarz gives L²≤k(L+gr(r−1)). The function L²/(L+c) increases for L>0 and c≥0, including r=1, and substitution gives exactly the displayed rational bound. Its denominator is positive and expansion followed by inversion gives the stated O_g(1) remainder. A dyadic difference determines the smaller exponent by its 2-adic valuation, then determines the larger exponent. Substituting g=1,r=4 gives k≥98/13, ruling out six counts for k=6. Direct sampling gives 4,1,3,0,2 at the five listed shifts. The inspected verify.py and verification_output.txt are finite consistency checks, not the basis of the infinite proof.

The all-size bound uses a second moment on blocks of distinct sizes, rather than applying the known minimum criterion. The finite dyadic upper side is independently elementary: six distinct counts force blocks of sizes at least five and four, which cannot fit on six sites with overlap at most one. This does not subsume the all-size estimate.
